source.text: Καὶ ἀναβαίνων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρέλαβεν τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς κατ’ ἰδίαν, καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: And going up Jesus to Jerusalem he took the twelve disciples aside by themselves, and on the way he said to them:

en.L: And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the twelve disciples aside by themselves, and on the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,
en.B: As Jesus was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way up to Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the twelve disciples aside, away from the others, and spoke to them as they walked.
en.R: Jesus was going up to Jerusalem. On the way, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve followers to a place away from the other people. He said to them,

es.L: Y subiendo Jesús a Jerusalén, tomó aparte a los doce discípulos, a solas, y en el camino les dijo:
es.B: Mientras Jesús subía a Jerusalén, llevó aparte a los doce discípulos, lejos de los demás, y les habló por el camino.
es.R: Jesús iba subiendo a Jerusalén. En el camino llevó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce seguidores a un lugar apartado de la demás gente. Les dijo:

fr.L: Et comme Jésus montait à Jérusalem, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit les douze disciples à part, et en chemin {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit :
fr.B: Comme Jésus montait à Jérusalem, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit les douze disciples à l’écart, loin des autres, et leur parla tout en marchant.
fr.R: Jésus montait vers Jérusalem. En chemin, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a emmené {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} douze disciples dans un endroit loin des autres gens. Il leur a dit :

sw.L: Na Yesu akiwa anapanda kwenda Yerusalemu, aliwachukua kando wanafunzi kumi na wawili peke yao, na walipokuwa njiani aliwaambia,
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa akipanda kwenda Yerusalemu, aliwachukua kando wale wanafunzi kumi na wawili, mbali na watu wengine, akazungumza nao walipokuwa wakitembea.
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa akienda Yerusalemu. Njiani aliwachukua wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili, akaenda nao mahali mbali na watu wengine. Akawaambia,

vi.L: Và khi đang đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem, Đức Giê-xu đem mười hai môn đồ riêng ra, và dọc đường {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ:
vi.B: Trên đường đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem, Đức Giê-xu đem mười hai môn đồ riêng ra, tách khỏi những người khác, và vừa đi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vừa nói với họ:
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đang đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Dọc đường, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đem mười hai môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến một chỗ riêng, cách xa những người khác. Ngài nói với họ:

decisions.choice: going up to Jerusalem: the city stood high in the hills
decisions.reason: Jerusalem lies high in the hill country, and travelers always spoke of going up to it. Jesus is now on the road from the Jordan valley (19:1; 20:29).

decisions.choice: aside by themselves: away from the crowds traveling with them
decisions.reason: Large crowds were following him (19:2; 20:29). This teaching is for the Twelve alone.

decisions.choice: the twelve disciples
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "disciples" and read "the Twelve". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: followers
decisions.reason: Readable says what disciples are, as in 5:1.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (lo, le, él, su, mi, tu)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("tomó", "les dijo") where English says "he", so there is nothing to capitalise; pronouns joined to the verb are also left plain. The setting therefore covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("elle lui dit", "ils lui disent")
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable tells the story in the passé composé, as French is spoken. Speech keeps its own tenses. Literal keeps the present where Matthew tells a past event in the present, as English Literal does. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: disciples at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers"; as in Mark and Luke, French keeps "les disciples" at every level, where the word is familiar and plain. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on the verbs (aliwachukua, aliwaambia); spans on free pronouns and possessives only
decisions.reason: The English "he" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the verb's subject prefix, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "mười hai môn đồ" at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek here says "the twelve disciples", not "the Twelve" alone, so the noun is kept at every level, Readable included.

source.text: Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ, καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εἰς τὸ ἐμπαῖξαι καὶ μαστιγῶσαι καὶ σταυρῶσαι, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Behold we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death \v 19 and they will hand over him to the Gentiles to mock and to flog and to crucify, and on the third day he will be raised.

en.L: "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death \v 19 and will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles to mock and to flog and to crucify, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised."
en.B: "We are going up to Jerusalem now. There the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will sentence {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death \v 19 and turn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to the Gentiles, who will mock {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, whip {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised to life."
en.R: "Listen! We are going up to Jerusalem. There the Son of Man will be handed over to the leading priests and the teachers of the law. They will decide that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must die. \v 19 Then they will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to people who are not Jews. Those people will make fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, beat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with whips, and nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross to die. But on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised from death."

es.L: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, subimos a Jerusalén, y el Hijo del Hombre será entregado a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a [los] escribas, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} condenarán a muerte, \v 19 y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregarán a los gentiles para escarnecer y azotar y crucificar; y al tercer día será resucitado».
es.B: «Ahora subimos a Jerusalén. Allí el Hijo del Hombre será entregado a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los escribas. Ellos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} condenarán a muerte \v 19 y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregarán a los gentiles, que se burlarán de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} azotarán y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} crucificarán. Y al tercer día será resucitado».
es.R: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Vamos subiendo a Jerusalén. Allí el Hijo del Hombre será entregado a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los maestros de la ley. Ellos decidirán que tiene que morir. \v 19 Después {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregarán a gente que no es judía. Esa gente se burlará de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} azotará con látigos y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} clavará en una cruz para que muera. Pero al tercer día será resucitado de la muerte».

fr.L: « Voici, nous montons à Jérusalem, et le Fils de l’homme sera livré aux chefs des prêtres et aux scribes, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} condamneront à mort \v 19 et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livreront aux nations pour se moquer [de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] flageller et [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] crucifier, et le troisième jour {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera ressuscité. »
fr.B: « Nous montons maintenant à Jérusalem. Là, le Fils de l’homme sera livré aux chefs des prêtres et aux scribes. Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} condamneront à mort \v 19 et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livreront aux non-Juifs, qui se moqueront de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fouetteront et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifieront. Et le troisième jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera ramené à la vie. »
fr.R: « Écoutez ! Nous montons à Jérusalem. Là, le Fils de l’homme sera livré aux chefs des prêtres et aux spécialistes de la Loi. Ils décideront qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} doit mourir. \v 19 Puis ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livreront à des gens qui ne sont pas juifs. Ces gens se moqueront de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} frapperont à coups de fouet et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} cloueront sur une croix pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} meure. Mais le troisième jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera ramené de la mort à la vie. »

sw.L: "Tazama, tunapanda kwenda Yerusalemu, na Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi, nao watamhukumu adhabu ya kifo, \v 19 na watamkabidhi kwa watu wa mataifa, ili kumfanyia dhihaka, na kumchapa viboko, na kumsulubisha; na siku ya tatu atafufuliwa."
sw.B: "Sasa tunapanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Huko Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi. Watamhukumu kifo, \v 19 na kumkabidhi kwa watu wa mataifa, nao watamdhihaki, watamchapa mijeledi na kumsulubisha. Na siku ya tatu atafufuliwa."
sw.R: "Sikilizeni! Tunakwenda Yerusalemu. Huko Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria. Wataamua kwamba ni lazima afe. \v 19 Kisha watamkabidhi kwa watu wasio Wayahudi. Watu hao watamcheka, watampiga kwa mijeledi, na kumpigilia misumari msalabani ili afe. Lakini siku ya tatu atafufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu."

vi.L: "Này, chúng ta đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem, và Con Người sẽ bị nộp cho các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo; họ sẽ kết án tử hình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} \v 19 và sẽ nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho dân ngoại để chế nhạo, đánh đòn và đóng đinh vào thập tự giá; và đến ngày thứ ba {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ được sống lại."
vi.B: "Bây giờ chúng ta đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Tại đó Con Người sẽ bị nộp cho các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo. Họ sẽ kết án tử hình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} \v 19 và giao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho dân ngoại. Dân ngoại sẽ chế nhạo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đánh đòn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào thập tự giá. Nhưng đến ngày thứ ba, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ được sống lại."
vi.R: "Hãy nghe đây! Chúng ta đang đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Ở đó Con Người sẽ bị nộp cho các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy dạy luật. Họ sẽ quyết định rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phải chết. \v 19 Rồi họ sẽ giao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho những người không phải là người Do Thái. Những người ấy sẽ chế giễu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đánh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bằng roi và đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên thập tự giá cho đến chết. Nhưng đến ngày thứ ba, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ được sống lại từ cõi chết."

decisions.choice: handed over: given into the power of others
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Judas betraying Jesus (10:4; 26:15) and of the leaders handing him to Pilate (27:2) and Pilate handing him to be crucified (27:26). The passive in 20:18 leaves open who hands him over, and in the end God's plan stands behind it (26:24).

decisions.choice: mock, flog, crucify: the Roman way of executing slaves and rebels
decisions.reason: This is the first time in Matthew that Jesus names crucifixion as the way he will die (compare 16:21; 17:22-23). Crucifixion was a Roman punishment, often after a flogging, as happened to Jesus (27:26-31).

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the Roman authorities
decisions.reason: Judea was under a Roman governor, and the Jewish council could not carry out an execution on its own (John 18:31). The leaders hand Jesus to Pilate (27:2).

decisions.choice: will be raised: God will raise him
alternatives: he will rise by his own power only
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, as in 16:21 and 17:23, and points to God as the one who raises him. It can also be read as "will rise".

decisions.choice: look (L); "now" (B); "Listen!" (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: leading priests; teachers of the law
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain names used in 2:4.

decisions.choice: nail him to a cross to die
decisions.reason: Readable says what crucifying is.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre; los jefes de los sacerdotes; los escribas (L, B), los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used throughout Matthew. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the Law, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the words addressed to the disciples ({{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} and onward)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres (every level); les scribes (L, B), les spécialistes de la Loi (R); les nations (L), les non-Juifs (B), des gens qui ne sont pas juifs (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The style guide's terms for the New Testament, as in Mark 10. "Les grands prêtres" would blur the line with "le grand prêtre" himself; Readable follows the English "teachers of the law"; "les païens" carries a judgment on religion that the Greek word for the nations does not.

decisions.choice: il sera ressuscité (L); il sera ramené à la vie (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew's verb is passive (m4: God will raise him), where Mark 10:34 has the active; French keeps the passive at every level so that God is the one who acts.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu; wakuu wa makuhani; waandishi (L, B), walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used throughout Matthew. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the Law, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa (L, B); watu wasio Wayahudi (R)
decisions.reason: "Mataifa" alone means the nations; "watu wa mataifa" is the usual Swahili for the Gentiles, here the Roman authorities (meaning decision m3). Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "các thầy tế lễ cả" at every level; "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B), "các thầy dạy luật" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled terms (Matthew 2:4, Mark 10:33).

decisions.choice: "dân ngoại" (L, B); "những người không phải là người Do Thái" (R); "đóng đinh vào thập tự giá"
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 10:5; Readable follows the English Readable here rather than naming the Romans as the Vietnamese Mark 10:33 does.

decisions.choice: "được sống lại" for the passive "will be raised"
decisions.reason: The Greek is passive here, unlike Mark 10:34; "được" keeps that God raises him.

source.text: Τότε προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου μετὰ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῆς προσκυνοῦσα καὶ αἰτοῦσά τι παρ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Then came to him the mother of the sons of Zebedee with the sons of her kneeling down and asking something from him.

en.L: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with her sons, kneeling down and asking something from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Then the mother of Zebedee's sons came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} together with her sons. She knelt in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a favor.
en.R: Then the mother of James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus with her sons. She bowed down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to do something for her.

es.L: Entonces vino a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} la madre de los hijos de Zebedeo con sus hijos, arrodillándose y solicitando algo de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Entonces la madre de los hijos de Zebedeo se acercó a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} junto con sus hijos. Se arrodilló delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pidió un favor.
es.R: Entonces la madre de Santiago y Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo, vino a ver a Jesús con sus hijos. Se inclinó delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pidió que hiciera algo por ella.

fr.L: Alors la mère des fils de Zébédée s’approcha de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avec ses fils, se prosternant et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandant quelque chose.
fr.B: Alors la mère des fils de Zébédée s’approcha de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avec ses fils. Elle se prosterna devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demander une faveur.
fr.R: Alors la mère de Jacques et de Jean, les fils de Zébédée, est venue voir Jésus avec ses fils. Elle s’est inclinée jusqu’à terre devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a demandé de faire quelque chose pour elle.

sw.L: Kisha mama wa wana wa Zebedayo akamjia pamoja na wanawe, akipiga magoti na kumwomba kitu.
sw.B: Kisha mama wa wana wa Zebedayo alimjia pamoja na wanawe. Akapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akamwomba amfanyie hisani.
sw.R: Kisha mama yao Yakobo na Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo, alimjia Yesu pamoja na wanawe. Akainama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akamwomba amfanyie jambo fulani.

vi.L: Bấy giờ mẹ của các con trai Xê-bê-đê cùng với các con trai mình đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, quỳ lạy và xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một điều.
vi.B: Bấy giờ mẹ của các con trai Xê-bê-đê cùng hai con mình đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Bà quỳ xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một ân huệ.
vi.R: Rồi mẹ của Gia-cơ và Giăng, hai con trai của ông Xê-bê-đê, cùng hai con đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. Bà quỳ xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm cho bà một việc.

decisions.choice: the mother of the sons of Zebedee: the mother of James and John
decisions.reason: Zebedee's sons are James and John (4:21; 10:2). Their mother is with the women at the cross (27:56). Mark 10:35 has the brothers make the request themselves; in Matthew their mother speaks for them, and Jesus answers the sons (20:22).

decisions.choice: kneeling down: bowing low in honor, as before a king
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow down before someone in honor. The magi did it before the child king (2:11). Her request is about his kingdom.

decisions.choice: James and John
decisions.reason: Readable names the sons, as 4:21 and 10:2 do.

decisions.choice: "quỳ lạy" (L); "quỳ xuống trước mặt" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the verb is the kneeling of a petitioner before one she honors; as in Matthew 15:25, not "thờ lạy" (worship).

decisions.choice: "Gia-cơ và Giăng" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable: the sons are named from Matthew 4:21 and 10:2.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Τί θέλεις;

records.literal_gloss: And he said to her, What do you desire?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "What do you want?"
en.B: "What is it you want?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked her.
en.R: Jesus asked her, "What do you want?"

es.B: «¿Qué es lo que quieres?», le preguntó.

fr.R: Jésus lui a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que tu veux ? »

vi.L: Ngài nói với bà: "Bà muốn gì?"
vi.B: Ngài hỏi bà: "Bà muốn điều gì?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi bà: "Bà muốn gì?"

decisions.choice: what do you want: an invitation to name the request
decisions.reason: Jesus asks her to say what she wants, as he asks the blind men in 20:32.

decisions.choice: Jesus calls the mother "bà"; she calls him "Thầy" and herself "tôi"
decisions.reason: An older woman, the mother of two disciples, speaking with respect to their teacher; as in Mark 10:35, her sons say "Thầy".

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ· Εἰπὲ ἵνα καθίσωσιν οὗτοι οἱ δύο υἱοί μου εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν σου καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων σου ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου.

records.literal_gloss: She says to him, Say that might sit these the two sons of me one on [the] right of you and one on [the] left of you in the kingdom of you.

en.L: She says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom."
en.B: She said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word that in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom these two sons of mine will sit beside {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right and one at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left."
en.R: She said, "Promise me that my two sons will sit next to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rule as king. Let one sit at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right side and the other at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} left side."

es.L: Ella {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «Di que estos dos hijos míos se sienten, uno a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} derecha y uno a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} izquierda, en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reino».
es.B: Ella {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Da {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} palabra de que en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reino estos dos hijos míos se sentarán junto a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, uno a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} derecha y el otro a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} izquierda».
es.R: Ella dijo: «Prométeme que mis dos hijos se sentarán a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lado cuando {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} gobiernes como rey. Que uno se siente a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} derecha y el otro a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} izquierda».

fr.L: Elle {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Dis que mes deux fils que voici siègent, l’un à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite et l’un à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gauche, dans {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} royaume. »
fr.B: Elle {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Donne-moi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} parole que, dans {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} royaume, mes deux fils que voici siégeront à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} côtés, l’un à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite et l’autre à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gauche. »
fr.R: Elle a répondu : « Promets-moi que mes deux fils seront assis à côté de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} régneras comme roi. Que l’un soit assis à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite et l’autre à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gauche. »

sw.L: Anamwambia, "Sema kwamba hawa wanangu wawili waketi, mmoja upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na mmoja upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}."
sw.B: Akamwambia, "Toa ahadi kwamba katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawa wanangu wawili wataketi karibu {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}, mmoja upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na mwingine upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}."
sw.R: Akasema, "Niahidi kwamba wanangu hawa wawili wataketi karibu {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} utakapotawala kama mfalme. Mmoja aketi upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na mwingine upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}."

vi.L: Bà nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Xin Thầy truyền cho hai con trai này của tôi được ngồi, một người bên phải Thầy và một người bên trái Thầy, trong vương quốc của Thầy."
vi.B: Bà thưa: "Xin Thầy hứa cho hai con trai tôi đây được ngồi bên cạnh Thầy trong vương quốc của Thầy, một người bên phải và một người bên trái."
vi.R: Bà thưa: "Xin Thầy hứa với tôi rằng khi Thầy làm Vua cai trị, hai con trai tôi sẽ được ngồi bên cạnh Thầy. Xin cho một đứa ngồi bên phải Thầy và một đứa ngồi bên trái Thầy."

decisions.choice: at your right and left: the places of highest honor beside a king
decisions.reason: The seat at a king's right hand was the place of greatest honor (1 Kings 2:19; Psalm 110:1). Jesus had just spoken of the Twelve sitting on thrones (19:28).

decisions.choice: say: give the word, decree it
decisions.reason: She asks Jesus to declare it as a king grants a request.

decisions.choice: right and left: perhaps looking ahead to the cross
decisions.reason: When Jesus is crucified as king of the Jews, two rebels hang beside him, one on his right and one on his left (27:37-38). Matthew may want readers to see the irony, but he does not say so.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: Give your word (B); Promise me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what she asks Jesus to say.

decisions.choice: when you rule as king
decisions.reason: Readable says what "your kingdom" means for her request.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (le dice); past at Balanced and Readable (le dijo)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of this story in the present (English decision r-en-1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell it in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in verses 22, 23 and 33.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (Anamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable (Akamwambia, Akasema)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of this story in the present (English decision r-en-1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past. The same in verses 22, 23 and 33.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "you" and "your", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the style guide says, a noun of address such as "Thầy" is always capitalised and takes no setting, even where the English has a span.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ μέλλω πίνειν;

records.literal_gloss: Answering now Jesus said, Not you know what you ask for; are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?

en.L: But Jesus answered and said, "You do not know what you are asking for. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?"
en.B: Jesus answered, "You do not realize what you are asking. The cup I am about to drink: are you able to drink it?"
en.R: Jesus answered, "You do not understand what you are asking for. I am going to drink a cup of suffering. Can you drink from that cup too?"

es.L: Pero Jesús respondió y dijo: «No {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} beber la copa que yo estoy a punto de beber?».
es.B: Jesús respondió: «No {{plural_you:se dan|os dais}} cuenta de lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. La copa que yo voy a beber, ¿{{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} beberla?».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «No {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}} lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. Yo voy a beber una copa de sufrimiento. ¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} beber también de esa copa?».

fr.L: Mais Jésus, répondant, dit : « Vous ne savez pas ce que vous demandez. Pouvez-vous boire la coupe que moi, je vais boire ? »
fr.B: Jésus répondit : « Vous ne savez pas ce que vous demandez. La coupe que je vais boire, pouvez-vous la boire ? »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Vous ne comprenez pas ce que vous demandez. Je vais boire une coupe de souffrance. Pouvez-vous boire, vous aussi, à cette coupe ? »

sw.L: Lakini Yesu alijibu, akasema, "Hamjui mnachokiomba. Je, mnaweza kunywa kikombe ambacho {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakaribia kukinywa?"
sw.B: Yesu alijibu, "Hamtambui mnachoomba. Kikombe ninachokaribia kunywa, je, mnaweza kukinywa?"
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Hamwelewi mnachoomba. Mimi nitakunywa kikombe cha mateso. Je, ninyi mnaweza kunywa katika kikombe hicho pia?"

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu đáp lời và nói: "Các con không biết điều mình xin. Các con có thể uống chén mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp uống không?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Các con không biết mình đang xin gì. Chén {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp uống, các con có uống nổi không?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Các con không hiểu điều mình đang xin. Ta sắp phải uống một chén đau khổ. Các con có thể uống chén ấy không?"

decisions.choice: the cup: the suffering God gives him to bear
decisions.reason: In the prophets the cup stands for God's judgment that the wicked must drink (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15; Psalm 75:8). In Gethsemane Jesus prays that this cup might pass from him (26:39).

decisions.choice: you: plural, the two brothers
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural. Jesus turns from the mother to the sons, who answer him.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends with the cup
alternatives: adds: or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a saying about baptism here and in 20:23, which appears to come from Mark 10:38-39. The earliest manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a cup of suffering
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup stands for.

decisions.choice: "vous" (plural) in Jesus's answer
decisions.reason: The mother asked, but Jesus answers the two brothers (m2), and the Greek verbs are plural; French "vous" here is the plural, as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: "các con" for the plural "you": Jesus answers the two sons
decisions.reason: The Greek turns to the plural; Jesus speaks to the brothers as "các con", as in Mark 10:38.

decisions.choice: "chén đau khổ" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable and the Vietnamese Mark 10:38: the cup is the suffering he must drink.

records.literal_gloss: They say to him, We are able.

fr.R: Ils ont dit : « Oui, nous le pouvons. »

vi.L: Họ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Chúng con có thể."
vi.R: Họ đáp: "Thưa được, chúng con làm được."

decisions.choice: we are able: a confident answer that they do not yet understand
alternatives: a true measure of their strength
decisions.reason: When Jesus is arrested, all the disciples leave him and run away (26:56).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: "nói" with no "đã" (L) for the historic present, also 20:21, 20:23 and 20:33
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Matthew.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τὸ μὲν ποτήριόν μου πίεσθε, τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου καὶ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου.

records.literal_gloss: He says to them, The indeed cup of me you will drink, but to sit on [the] right of me and on [the] left not is mine to give, but [to those] for whom it has been prepared by the Father of me.

en.L: He says to them, "My cup you will indeed drink, but to sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right and at [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}}] left is not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} to give, but [it is for those] for whom it has been prepared by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father."
en.B: He told them, "You will indeed drink {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} cup. But the places at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right and left are not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} to hand out. They belong to those for whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father has prepared them."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Yes, you will drink from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} cup of suffering. But I am not the one who chooses who will sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right side or {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} left side. My Father has made those places ready, and they are for the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them ready for."

es.L: Les dice: «Mi copa, ciertamente, la {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}}; pero el sentarse a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha y a [{{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}}] izquierda no es cosa {{deity_pronoun:mía|Mía}} concederlo, sino [que es para aquellos] para quienes ha sido preparado por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre».
es.B: Él les dijo: «Es cierto que {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} copa. Pero los lugares a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha y a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} izquierda no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} toca a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} repartirlos. Son para aquellos para quienes {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre los ha preparado».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Sí, {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}} de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} copa de sufrimiento. Pero no soy yo quien decide quién se sentará a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} derecha o a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} izquierda. Mi Padre ha preparado esos lugares, y son para las personas para quienes {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los preparó».

fr.L: Il leur dit : « Ma coupe, vous la boirez en effet ; mais siéger à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} droite et à [{{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}}] gauche, il ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartient pas de le donner, mais [c’est] pour ceux pour qui cela a été préparé par {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père. »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Vous boirez bien {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} coupe. Mais les places à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} droite et à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} gauche, ce n’est pas à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} de les attribuer. Elles sont à ceux pour qui {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père les a préparées. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Oui, vous boirez à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} coupe de souffrance. Mais ce n’est pas {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui choisis qui sera assis à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} droite ou à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} gauche. Mon Père a préparé ces places, et elles sont pour ceux qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisis. »

sw.L: Anawaambia, "Kweli kikombe {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} mtakinywa, lakini kuketi upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} na wa kushoto si kazi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kukitoa, bali [ni kwa wale] ambao kimeandaliwa kwa ajili yao na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}."
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Hakika mtakinywa kikombe {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}. Lakini nafasi za upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} na wa kushoto si kazi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuzigawa. Ni za wale ambao Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} amewaandalia."
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Ndiyo, mtakunywa katika kikombe {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} cha mateso. Lakini si {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninayechagua nani ataketi upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} au upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ameandaa nafasi hizo, nazo ni za wale aliowaandalia."

vi.L: Ngài nói với họ: "Chén của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì các con sẽ uống, nhưng việc ngồi bên phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và bên trái [{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}] thì không phải [quyền] của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho, nhưng [là] cho những người mà Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã dọn sẵn."
vi.B: Ngài bảo họ: "Chén của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì các con sẽ uống. Nhưng chỗ ngồi bên phải và bên trái {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là người ban cho. Những chỗ ấy thuộc về những người mà Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã dọn sẵn cho họ."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Đúng vậy, các con sẽ uống chén đau khổ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không phải là người chọn ai sẽ ngồi bên phải hay bên trái {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã dọn sẵn những chỗ ấy, và những chỗ ấy dành cho những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã dọn sẵn cho."

decisions.choice: you will drink my cup: they will share his suffering
decisions.reason: Jesus promises them suffering, not seats of honor. Herod Agrippa later put James to death with the sword (Acts 12:2).

decisions.choice: prepared by my Father: the Father decides who has those places
decisions.reason: Jesus leaves the places of honor to his Father, as he leaves the day of the end to him (24:36).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: I am not the one who chooses
decisions.reason: Readable says what giving the places means.

source.text: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἠγανάκτησαν περὶ τῶν δύο ἀδελφῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard the ten were indignant about the two brothers.

en.L: And when the ten heard [it], they became indignant about the two brothers.
en.B: The other ten were furious with the two brothers when they heard of this.
en.R: The other ten followers heard about this, and they were angry with the two brothers.

es.L: Y habiendo oído [esto], los diez se indignaron por los dos hermanos.
es.B: Cuando los otros diez se enteraron, se enfurecieron con los dos hermanos.
es.R: Los otros diez seguidores se enteraron de esto, y se enojaron con los dos hermanos.

fr.L: Et ayant entendu [cela], les dix s’indignèrent contre les deux frères.
fr.B: Quand les dix autres l’apprirent, ils furent indignés contre les deux frères.
fr.R: Les dix autres disciples ont appris cela, et ils se sont fâchés contre les deux frères.

sw.L: Na waliposikia, wale kumi walighadhibika kwa ajili ya ndugu wale wawili.
sw.B: Wale wanafunzi kumi wengine waliposikia jambo hilo, waliwakasirikia sana wale ndugu wawili.
sw.R: Wale wafuasi wengine kumi walisikia habari hii, wakawakasirikia wale ndugu wawili.

vi.L: Và mười [người kia] nghe [vậy] thì bất bình với hai anh em ấy.
vi.B: Khi mười môn đồ kia nghe chuyện này, họ rất bực tức với hai anh em ấy.
vi.R: Mười môn đồ kia nghe biết chuyện này. Họ giận hai anh em ấy.

decisions.choice: were indignant: angry at what they saw as wrong
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the chief priests in 21:15 and of the disciples in 26:8. The ten seem as eager for honor as the two.

decisions.choice: the other ten
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the ten are the rest of the Twelve.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus having called to [him] them said, You know that the rulers of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them and the great ones exercise authority over them.

en.L: But Jesus called them to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and said, "You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and the great ones exercise authority over them.
en.B: Jesus called them together and said, "You know that among the Gentiles, rulers act as lords over their people, and the powerful wield their authority over them.
en.R: Jesus called them all together and said to them, "You know about the kings and rulers of other nations. They act like masters over the people they rule. Their important leaders use their power to control them.

es.L: Pero Jesús, llamándolos a [{{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}}], dijo: «{{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que los gobernantes de los gentiles se hacen señores de ellos, y los grandes ejercen su autoridad sobre ellos.
es.B: Jesús los llamó y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que entre los gentiles los gobernantes actúan como amos de sus pueblos, y los poderosos les imponen su autoridad.
es.R: Jesús los llamó a todos y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} cómo son los reyes y gobernantes de otras naciones. Se portan como amos de la gente que gobiernan. Sus jefes importantes usan su poder para dominarla.

fr.L: Mais Jésus, les ayant appelés auprès [de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], dit : « Vous savez que les chefs des nations dominent sur elles en seigneurs, et que les grands exercent sur elles leur autorité.
fr.B: Jésus les appela auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et leur dit : « Vous savez que chez les non-Juifs, les chefs dominent leurs peuples en maîtres, et que les puissants font peser sur eux leur autorité.
fr.R: Jésus les a tous appelés et leur a dit : « Vous savez comment font les rois et les chefs des autres nations. Ils se conduisent en maîtres avec les gens qu’ils gouvernent. Leurs grands chefs se servent de leur pouvoir pour les dominer.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu aliwaita, akasema, "Mnajua kwamba watawala wa watu wa mataifa huwatawala kama mabwana, na wakubwa hutumia mamlaka juu yao.
sw.B: Yesu aliwaita pamoja, akasema, "Mnajua kwamba kwa watu wa mataifa, watawala hujifanya mabwana juu ya watu wao, na wenye nguvu huwatawala kwa mamlaka yao.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaita wote pamoja, akawaambia, "Mnajua habari za wafalme na watawala wa mataifa mengine. Wao hujifanya mabwana juu ya watu wanaowatawala. Viongozi wao wakubwa hutumia nguvu zao kuwadhibiti.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu gọi họ lại [với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] và nói: "Các con biết rằng những người cai trị các dân ngoại thì thống trị họ, và những người lớn thì dùng quyền lực trên họ.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu gọi họ lại và bảo: "Các con biết rằng giữa các dân ngoại, những người cai trị thì làm chủ dân mình, và những kẻ quyền thế thì dùng quyền lực đè nén dân.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu gọi tất cả các môn đồ lại và nói với họ: "Các con biết các vua chúa và những người cai trị các dân tộc khác là thế nào rồi. Họ làm như mình là chủ của dân họ cai trị. Những người lãnh đạo quan trọng của họ dùng quyền lực để kiểm soát dân chúng.

decisions.choice: lord it over, exercise authority over: rule harshly, using power for themselves
decisions.reason: Both verbs are strengthened forms of the words for ruling and having authority. They suggest power used against those under it.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the nations of the world and their rulers
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of how kings and governors of the nations rule, as Rome ruled at that time.

decisions.choice: called them: all twelve
decisions.reason: Jesus calls the whole group, both the two and the angry ten.

decisions.choice: act like masters over
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: the speech runs on to 20:28
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer runs to the end of 20:28, so the quotation opens here and closes there.

source.text: οὐχ οὕτως ἔσται ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλ’ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν μέγας γενέσθαι ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος, καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος ἔσται ὑμῶν δοῦλος·

records.literal_gloss: Not thus will it be among you; but whoever wishes among you great to become will be your servant, \v 27 and whoever wishes among you to be first will be your slave;

en.L: It will not be so among you; but whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant, \v 27 and whoever wants to be first among you will be your slave,
en.B: With you it must be different. If any of you wants to become great, that one must serve the rest of you. \v 27 And if any of you wants to be first, that one must be your slave.
en.R: But it must not be like that with you. If anyone among you wants to be great, that person must serve the others. \v 27 If anyone wants to be first, that person must be your slave.

es.L: Entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no será así; al contrario, quien quiera hacerse grande entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} será {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} sirviente, \v 27 y quien quiera ser primero entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} será {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} esclavo,
es.B: Entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tiene que ser distinto. Si alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quiere llegar a ser grande, deberá servir a los demás. \v 27 Y si alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quiere ser el primero, deberá ser {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} esclavo.
es.R: Pero entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no debe ser así. Si alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quiere ser grande, debe servir a los demás. \v 27 Si alguien quiere ser el primero, debe ser {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} esclavo.

fr.L: Il n’en sera pas ainsi parmi vous ; mais quiconque veut devenir grand parmi vous sera votre serviteur, \v 27 et quiconque veut être le premier parmi vous sera votre esclave,
fr.B: Parmi vous, il doit en être autrement. Si l’un de vous veut devenir grand, qu’il soit le serviteur des autres. \v 27 Et si l’un de vous veut être le premier, qu’il soit votre esclave.
fr.R: Mais chez vous, ce ne doit pas être comme cela. Si quelqu’un parmi vous veut être grand, il doit servir les autres. \v 27 Si quelqu’un veut être le premier, il doit être votre esclave.

sw.L: Kati yenu haitakuwa hivyo; bali yule atakayetaka kuwa mkuu kati yenu atakuwa mhudumu wenu, \v 27 na yule atakayetaka kuwa wa kwanza kati yenu atakuwa mtumwa wenu,
sw.B: Kwenu ni lazima iwe tofauti. Mtu yeyote kati yenu akitaka kuwa mkuu, ni lazima awahudumie wengine. \v 27 Na mtu yeyote kati yenu akitaka kuwa wa kwanza, ni lazima awe mtumwa wenu.
sw.R: Lakini kwenu isiwe hivyo. Mtu yeyote kati yenu akitaka kuwa mkubwa, ni lazima awatumikie wengine. \v 27 Mtu yeyote akitaka kuwa wa kwanza, ni lazima awe mtumwa wenu.

vi.L: Giữa các con thì không như vậy; trái lại, ai muốn trở nên lớn giữa các con thì sẽ là người phục vụ các con, \v 27 và ai muốn đứng đầu giữa các con thì sẽ là nô lệ của các con;
vi.B: Giữa các con thì phải khác. Ai trong các con muốn làm lớn thì phải làm người phục vụ các con, \v 27 và ai trong các con muốn đứng đầu thì phải làm nô lệ cho các con.
vi.R: Nhưng giữa các con thì không được như thế. Nếu ai trong các con muốn làm lớn, người ấy phải phục vụ những người khác. \v 27 Nếu ai muốn đứng đầu, người ấy phải làm nô lệ cho các con.

decisions.choice: will not be, will be: futures that work as commands
decisions.reason: As in the law ("you shall not"), the future tells what must be among Jesus's followers.

decisions.choice: servant: one who waits on others
decisions.reason: The word was used of those who served at table and did the work others needed.

decisions.choice: slave: one owned by another, with no standing of his own
decisions.reason: The word is stronger than "servant". A slave belonged to a master. Jesus asks those who would be first to take the lowest place.

decisions.choice: will be
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "it is not so among you", as in Mark 10:43. The sense differs little. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: must
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the force of command.

decisions.choice: If any of you wants ..., that one must ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the relative clause into a condition, which reads more easily aloud.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where the word for slave stands against the word for servant in one saying: the step down from servant to slave is the point (m3).

decisions.choice: esclavo at every level
decisions.reason: As in English (r-en-3): the saying sets the slave, who has no standing of his own (meaning decision m3), against the great and the first, so "esclavo" is kept rather than the softer "siervo".

decisions.choice: serviteur ... esclave at every level
alternatives: serviteur ... serviteur at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As the English and Mark 10:43-44: the step down from servant to slave is the point (m3), so "esclave" stands at every level, as the style guide allows where slavery itself is meant.

decisions.choice: mhudumu (L), awahudumie (B) for the servant; mtumwa at every level for the slave
decisions.reason: The servant is one who waits on others (meaning decision m2), which "kuhudumia" says. The slave has no standing of his own (meaning decision m3), and the saying turns on that, so "mtumwa" is kept at every level, as the English keeps "slave" (r-en-3), rather than the softer "mtumishi".

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" at every level, beside "người phục vụ"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 10:43-44 and the English style guide: the step down from servant to slave is the point of the saying, so "nô lệ" stays at every level.

source.text: ὥσπερ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.

records.literal_gloss: even as the Son of Man not came to be served but to serve and to give the life of him a ransom for many.

en.L: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life [as] a ransom for many."
en.B: It is the same with the Son of Man. He did not come so that others would wait on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He came to serve them, and to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as a ransom for many."
en.R: Be like the Son of Man. He did not come so that people would serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He came to serve other people. He came to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life as a ransom, a price paid to set many people free."

es.L: así como el Hijo del Hombre no vino a ser servido, sino a servir, y a dar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida [como] rescate a cambio de muchos».
es.B: Así es también con el Hijo del Hombre. No vino para que otros {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} atendieran. Vino a servirles y a dar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida como rescate por muchos».
es.R: {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} como el Hijo del Hombre. No vino para que la gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} sirviera. Vino a servir a los demás. Vino a dar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida como rescate, un precio pagado para dejar libres a muchas personas».

fr.L: de même que le Fils de l’homme n’est pas venu pour être servi, mais pour servir et pour donner {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie [en] rançon pour beaucoup. »
fr.B: Il en va de même pour le Fils de l’homme. Il n’est pas venu pour que d’autres {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servent. Il est venu pour les servir et pour donner {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie en rançon pour un grand nombre. »
fr.R: Faites comme le Fils de l’homme. Il n’est pas venu pour que les gens {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servent. Il est venu pour servir les autres. Il est venu donner {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie comme rançon, c’est-à-dire le prix payé pour libérer beaucoup de gens. »

sw.L: sawa na Mwana wa Adamu, ambaye hakuja ili ahudumiwe bali ahudumie, na kutoa uhai {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} [uwe] fidia badala ya wengi."
sw.B: Ndivyo ilivyo kwa Mwana wa Adamu. Hakuja ili wengine wamhudumie. Alikuja kuwahudumia, na kutoa uhai {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kuwa fidia kwa ajili ya wengi."
sw.R: Iweni kama Mwana wa Adamu. Hakuja ili watu wamtumikie. Alikuja kuwatumikia wengine. Alikuja kutoa uhai {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kuwa fidia, yaani gharama inayolipwa ili watu wengi wawe huru."

vi.L: cũng như Con Người đã không đến để được phục vụ, nhưng để phục vụ và hiến mạng sống mình [làm] giá chuộc cho nhiều người."
vi.B: Con Người cũng vậy: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đến, không phải để được người ta phục vụ, nhưng để phục vụ họ và hiến mạng sống mình làm giá chuộc cho nhiều người."
vi.R: Hãy giống như Con Người. Ngài không đến để được người ta phục vụ. Ngài đến để phục vụ người khác. Ngài đến để hiến mạng sống mình làm giá chuộc, tức là cái giá phải trả để giải phóng nhiều người."

decisions.choice: ransom: the price paid to set a slave or captive free
decisions.reason: The word was used of money paid to free a slave or prisoner (Leviticus 25:51-52) and of a payment that saved a life that was forfeit (Exodus 21:30; 30:12). Jesus gives his own life as that price.

decisions.choice: for many: in place of many, for a great number
decisions.reason: The preposition commonly means "in place of" or "in exchange for". "Many" sets the great number who are freed against the one who gives his life; it does not mean that others are left out (compare Isaiah 53:11-12).

decisions.choice: his death sets many free at the cost of his life
decisions.reason: Jesus's death is more than an example: it pays for the freedom of many. Matthew does not say to whom the ransom is paid. At the Last Supper Jesus speaks of his blood poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins (26:28).

decisions.choice: the servant of Isaiah 53
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:10-12 tells of the servant whose life is made an offering for sin and who bears the sin of many. The word "ransom" is not in Isaiah 53, and some hear instead the language of God freeing his people from slavery (Deuteronomy 7:8).

decisions.choice: It is the same with the Son of Man
alternatives: just as the Son of Man
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long sentence and makes the link to 20:26-27 a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: Be like the Son of Man
alternatives: just as the Son of Man
decisions.reason: The words "just as" make the Son of Man the pattern for the disciples. Readable says so directly.

decisions.choice: a ransom, a price paid to set many people free
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a ransom is in a short added phrase.

decisions.choice: a cambio de muchos
decisions.reason: The preposition means "in place of" (meaning decision m2); "a cambio de" keeps the exchange that a ransom is. Balanced and Readable use the plainer "por".

decisions.choice: uhai
decisions.reason: The Greek word can mean soul or life; here it is his life, given up in death (meaning decision m3). "Uhai" is life itself; "nafsi" would suggest the soul.

decisions.choice: badala ya wengi
decisions.reason: The preposition means "in place of" (meaning decision m2), which "badala ya" says exactly. Balanced and Readable use the plainer "kwa ajili ya".

decisions.choice: "hiến mạng sống mình [làm] giá chuộc" (L); "làm giá chuộc" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the Vietnamese Mark 10:45, of which this is the parallel; "mạng sống" for psychē.

source.text: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.

records.literal_gloss: And going out them from Jericho followed him a crowd great.

en.L: And as they were going out from Jericho, a large crowd followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: A large crowd went along behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} and the disciples left Jericho.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were leaving the town of Jericho. A large crowd of people followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y mientras ellos salían de Jericó, una gran multitud {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió.
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y los discípulos salían de Jericó, una gran multitud iba tras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores estaban saliendo del pueblo de Jericó. Una gran multitud de gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguía.

fr.L: Et comme ils sortaient de Jéricho, une grande foule {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivit.
fr.B: Comme Jésus et les disciples quittaient Jéricho, une grande foule {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivit.
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples quittaient la ville de Jéricho. Une grande foule {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a suivi.

sw.L: Nao walipokuwa wakiondoka Yeriko, umati mkubwa ulimfuata.
sw.B: Alipokuwa akiondoka Yeriko pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, umati mkubwa wa watu ulifuata nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Yesu na wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakitoka katika mji wa Yeriko. Umati mkubwa wa watu ukamfuata.

vi.L: Và khi họ ra khỏi Giê-ri-cô, có một đoàn dân đông đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ ra khỏi Giê-ri-cô, có một đoàn dân đông đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang rời thành Giê-ri-cô. Có rất đông người đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: Jericho: a town in the Jordan valley, the last stop before the climb to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jericho lay near the Jordan, about fifteen miles northeast of Jerusalem and far below it. Travelers from Galilee by the Jordan road went up to Jerusalem from there.

decisions.choice: they: Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: The pronoun takes up Jesus and the Twelve from 20:17.

decisions.choice: he and the disciples (B); Jesus and his followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο τυφλοὶ καθήμενοι παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ἰησοῦς παράγει, ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὸς Δαυίδ.

records.literal_gloss: And behold two blind sitting beside the road, having heard that Jesus is passing by, cried out saying, Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.

en.L: And look, two blind [men] sitting beside the road, hearing that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!"
en.B: Beside the road sat two blind men. They heard that Jesus was passing, and they began to shout, "Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!"
en.R: Two blind men were sitting beside the road. They heard that Jesus was going past, so they shouted, "Lord, Son of David, please have pity on us!"

es.L: Y mira, dos ciegos [que estaban] sentados junto al camino, al oír que Jesús pasaba, gritaron diciendo: «¡Señor, ten piedad de nosotros, Hijo de David!».
es.B: Junto al camino estaban sentados dos ciegos. Oyeron que Jesús pasaba y se pusieron a gritar: «¡Ten piedad de nosotros, Señor, Hijo de David!».
es.R: Dos ciegos estaban sentados al lado del camino. Oyeron que Jesús pasaba por allí, y gritaron: «¡Señor, Hijo de David, por favor, ten compasión de nosotros!».

fr.L: Et voici, deux aveugles assis au bord du chemin, entendant que Jésus passait, crièrent, disant : « Seigneur, aie pitié de nous, Fils de David ! »
fr.B: Au bord de la route étaient assis deux aveugles. Apprenant que Jésus passait, ils se mirent à crier : « Aie pitié de nous, Seigneur, Fils de David ! »
fr.R: Deux aveugles étaient assis au bord de la route. Ils ont entendu que Jésus passait par là. Alors ils ont crié : « Seigneur, Fils de David, aie pitié de nous, s’il te plaît ! »

sw.L: Na tazama, vipofu wawili waliokuwa wamekaa kando ya barabara, waliposikia kuwa Yesu anapita, walilia kwa sauti wakisema, "Bwana, tuhurumie, Mwana wa Daudi!"
sw.B: Kando ya njia walikuwa wameketi vipofu wawili. Walisikia kwamba Yesu anapita, wakaanza kupaza sauti, "Tuhurumie, Bwana, Mwana wa Daudi!"
sw.R: Vipofu wawili walikuwa wameketi kando ya njia. Walisikia kwamba Yesu anapita, basi wakapiga kelele, "Bwana, Mwana wa Daudi, tafadhali tuonee huruma!"

vi.L: Và kìa, có hai người mù ngồi bên đường, nghe nói Đức Giê-xu đang đi ngang qua, thì kêu lên rằng: "Lạy Chúa, xin thương xót chúng con, Con của Đa-vít!"
vi.B: Có hai người mù đang ngồi bên vệ đường. Nghe nói Đức Giê-xu đang đi ngang qua, họ liền kêu lên: "Lạy Chúa, Con của Đa-vít, xin thương xót chúng con!"
vi.R: Có hai người mù đang ngồi bên vệ đường. Họ nghe nói Đức Giê-xu đang đi ngang qua, nên kêu lớn: "Lạy Chúa, Con vua Đa-vít, xin thương xót chúng con!"

decisions.choice: Son of David: a title for the promised king
decisions.reason: As in 9:27, the title names Jesus as the Messiah (1:1; 2 Samuel 7:12-16). The prophets said the blind would see when God came to save (Isaiah 35:5). Jesus is about to enter Jerusalem as the Son of David (21:9).

decisions.choice: two blind men
decisions.reason: As in 9:27 and 8:28, Matthew tells of two. Mark 10:46 names one of them, Bartimaeus.

decisions.choice: Lord, have mercy on us
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here: some lack "Lord", and some have "Jesus" in its place. The SBLGNT reads "Lord", as all agree in 20:31. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); absorbed (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: please have pity on us
decisions.reason: As in 9:27, Readable uses plain words for the cry.

decisions.choice: ten piedad (L, B); ten compasión (R)
decisions.reason: A cry for help from someone able to give it. "Ten piedad" is the plain, living form of that plea; Readable uses the everyday "compasión", as the English Readable says "pity".

decisions.choice: Seigneur ... aie pitié de nous; "tu" to Jesus
decisions.reason: The men call on Jesus as the Son of David, the promised king (m1), so French says "Seigneur", as in Mark 10:47, and addresses him with "tu", as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: tuhurumie (L, B); tuonee huruma (R)
decisions.reason: The blind men ask for pity that acts to help them. "Kuhurumia" is the everyday word for that and suits a cry from the roadside; Readable uses the plainer "kuonea huruma".

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa", "Con của Đa-vít" (L, B), "Con vua Đa-vít" (R), with "chúng con" for the blind men
decisions.reason: As for the two blind men of Matthew 9:27-28.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σιωπήσωσιν· οἱ δὲ μεῖζον ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὸς Δαυίδ.

records.literal_gloss: And the crowd rebuked them that they should be silent; but they more cried out saying, Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.

en.L: And the crowd rebuked them, that they should be silent; but they cried out all the more, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!"
en.B: The crowd scolded them and told them to keep quiet, but they only shouted louder, "Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!"
en.R: The people in the crowd told them off and said they must be quiet. But the men shouted even louder, "Lord, Son of David, please have pity on us!"

es.L: Pero la multitud los increpó para que guardaran silencio; ellos, sin embargo, gritaron todavía más, diciendo: «¡Señor, ten piedad de nosotros, Hijo de David!».
es.B: La multitud los regañó y les dijo que se callaran, pero ellos gritaban aún más fuerte: «¡Ten piedad de nosotros, Señor, Hijo de David!».
es.R: La gente de la multitud los reprendió y les dijo que se callaran. Pero los hombres gritaron todavía más fuerte: «¡Señor, Hijo de David, por favor, ten compasión de nosotros!».

fr.L: Et la foule les reprit sévèrement pour qu’ils se taisent ; mais eux crièrent plus fort, disant : « Seigneur, aie pitié de nous, Fils de David ! »
fr.B: La foule les rabroua et leur dit de se taire, mais ils crièrent encore plus fort : « Aie pitié de nous, Seigneur, Fils de David ! »
fr.R: Les gens de la foule les ont grondés et leur ont dit de se taire. Mais les deux hommes ont crié encore plus fort : « Seigneur, Fils de David, aie pitié de nous, s’il te plaît ! »

sw.L: Na umati ukawakaripia wanyamaze; lakini wao wakalia kwa sauti kubwa zaidi, wakisema, "Bwana, tuhurumie, Mwana wa Daudi!"
sw.B: Umati uliwakaripia na kuwaambia wanyamaze, lakini wao wakapiga kelele zaidi, "Tuhurumie, Bwana, Mwana wa Daudi!"
sw.R: Watu wa umati waliwakemea, wakawaambia wanyamaze. Lakini wale watu wakapiga kelele kwa nguvu zaidi, "Bwana, Mwana wa Daudi, tafadhali tuonee huruma!"

vi.L: Đoàn dân quở trách họ, bảo họ im lặng; nhưng họ càng kêu lớn hơn: "Lạy Chúa, xin thương xót chúng con, Con của Đa-vít!"
vi.B: Đám đông rầy la, bảo họ im đi, nhưng họ càng kêu lớn hơn nữa: "Lạy Chúa, Con của Đa-vít, xin thương xót chúng con!"
vi.R: Đám đông la họ và bảo họ phải im lặng. Nhưng hai người càng kêu to hơn: "Lạy Chúa, Con vua Đa-vít, xin thương xót chúng con!"

decisions.choice: rebuked: sternly told them to stop
decisions.reason: The disciples rebuked those who brought children in the same way (19:13). The crowd thinks the blind men are not worth Jesus's time.

decisions.choice: cried out all the more: louder and more urgently
decisions.reason: The word means more, or louder. The men will not be silenced.

decisions.choice: Lord, Son of David, please have pity on us
alternatives: Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David
decisions.reason: Readable gives the cry in the same words as in 20:30.

source.text: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐφώνησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν· Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: And having stopped Jesus called them and said, What do you desire I should do to you?

en.L: And Jesus stopped, called them, and said, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"
en.B: Jesus stood still and called to them. "What would you like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked.
en.R: Jesus stopped and called the men. He asked them, "What do you want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do for you?"

es.L: Y Jesús, habiéndose detenido, los llamó y dijo: «¿Qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que haga por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?».
es.B: Jesús se detuvo y los llamó. «¿Qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que haga por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?», les preguntó.
es.R: Jesús se detuvo y llamó a los hombres. Les preguntó: «¿Qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que haga por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?».

fr.L: Et Jésus, s’étant arrêté, les appela et dit : « Que voulez-vous que je fasse pour vous ? »
fr.B: Jésus s’arrêta et les appela. « Que voulez-vous que je fasse pour vous ? » leur demanda-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}.
fr.R: Jésus s’est arrêté et il a appelé les deux hommes. Il leur a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que vous voulez que je fasse pour vous ? »

sw.L: Na Yesu, aliposimama, aliwaita na kusema, "Mnataka {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niwafanyie nini?"
sw.B: Yesu alisimama, akawaita. Akawauliza, "Mngependa niwafanyie nini?"
sw.R: Yesu alisimama, akawaita wale watu. Akawauliza, "Mnataka niwafanyie nini?"

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu dừng lại, gọi họ và nói: "Các anh muốn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm gì cho các anh?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đứng lại và gọi họ. Ngài hỏi: "Các anh muốn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm gì cho các anh?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu dừng bước và gọi hai người ấy. Ngài hỏi họ: "Các anh muốn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm gì cho các anh?"

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do: an invitation to ask
alternatives: Jesus does not know their need
decisions.reason: Jesus asks them to say what they want, using nearly the same words he used to the mother of James and John (20:21).

decisions.choice: stopped: Jesus halts for them while the crowd moves on
decisions.reason: The crowd wanted them silent; Jesus stops the whole procession for them.

decisions.choice: "các anh" for the two blind men
decisions.reason: As Jesus speaks to Bartimaeus in Mark 10:51; they are strangers, not disciples.

source.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἵνα ἀνοιγῶσιν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: They say to him, Lord, that might be opened the eyes of us.

en.L: They say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, [we want] our eyes to be opened."
en.B: "Lord," they replied, "we want our eyes to be opened."
en.R: They said, "Lord, we want to be able to see!"

es.L: Le dicen: «Señor, que sean abiertos nuestros ojos».
es.B: «Señor —le respondieron—, queremos que se abran nuestros ojos».

fr.L: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Seigneur, que nos yeux soient ouverts ! »
fr.B: « Seigneur, répondirent-ils, nous voulons que nos yeux s’ouvrent. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Seigneur, nous voulons pouvoir voir ! »

vi.L: Họ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa, [xin cho] mắt chúng con được mở ra."
vi.B: Họ thưa: "Lạy Chúa, xin cho mắt chúng con được mở ra."
vi.R: Họ thưa: "Lạy Chúa, chúng con muốn được nhìn thấy!"

decisions.choice: our eyes opened: to be given sight
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual one for giving sight to the blind (9:30).

decisions.choice: that: a request with the verb understood
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves "we want" unsaid; it answers the question in 20:32.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: we want
decisions.reason: English needs the verb that the Greek leaves understood. Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: que sean abiertos nuestros ojos, with no supplied words
decisions.reason: Spanish "que" with the subjunctive is itself a request, as the Greek is (meaning decision m2), so Literal needs no bracketed "[we want]" as the English does.

decisions.choice: que nos yeux soient ouverts ! (L), with no bracketed verb
alternatives: [nous voulons que] nos yeux soient ouverts
decisions.reason: French can say the wish with "que" and the subjunctive alone, just as the Greek leaves the verb of wishing understood (m2), so Literal needs no supplied words where English brackets "we want".

source.text: σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἥψατο τῶν ὀμμάτων αὐτῶν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέβλεψαν καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Having been moved with compassion then Jesus touched the eyes of them, and immediately they received sight and they followed him.

en.L: And having compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and immediately they received sight and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Jesus felt deep pity for them and touched their eyes. At once they could see, and they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus felt sorry for them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched their eyes. Right away they could see again. And they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y movido a compasión, Jesús tocó los ojos de ellos, y al instante recobraron la vista y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.
es.B: Jesús sintió profunda compasión por ellos y les tocó los ojos. Al momento pudieron ver, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.
es.R: Jesús sintió lástima por ellos y les tocó los ojos. Enseguida pudieron ver otra vez. Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.

fr.L: Et, pris de compassion, Jésus toucha leurs yeux, et aussitôt ils recouvrèrent la vue et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent.
fr.B: Jésus fut ému de compassion pour eux et toucha leurs yeux. Aussitôt ils virent, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent.
fr.R: Jésus a eu pitié d’eux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a touché leurs yeux. Tout de suite, ils ont pu voir de nouveau. Et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont suivi.

sw.L: Na Yesu, akiwa ameguswa moyoni kwa huruma, aligusa macho yao, na mara moja wakapata kuona, wakamfuata.
sw.B: Yesu aliwaonea huruma kubwa, akayagusa macho yao. Mara moja wakaweza kuona, nao wakamfuata.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaonea huruma, akayagusa macho yao. Mara moja wakaweza kuona tena. Nao wakamfuata.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu động lòng thương xót, chạm vào mắt họ, và lập tức họ thấy lại được và đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu động lòng thương xót sâu xa và chạm vào mắt họ. Ngay lúc đó họ thấy lại được, và họ đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu thương họ và chạm vào mắt họ. Ngay lập tức họ nhìn thấy lại được. Và họ đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: having compassion: moved deep within
decisions.reason: As in 9:36, the verb comes from the word for the inner organs, thought of as the seat of feeling. It is used in the Gospels almost only of Jesus (14:14; 15:32).

decisions.choice: eyes: a different word from the one in 20:33, with the same meaning
alternatives: a different part of the face
decisions.reason: Matthew uses a less common word for eyes here. It does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: they followed him: they went with him, perhaps as disciples
alternatives: they only walked along with the crowd
decisions.reason: "Follow" is Matthew's word for discipleship (4:20, 22; 9:9), but it is also used of crowds who walk with Jesus (20:29). The healed men go with Jesus up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: they received sight
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "their eyes" after the verb. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: felt deep pity (B); felt sorry (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as in 9:36.

decisions.choice: "lập tức" (L) for "immediately"
decisions.reason: The settled Literal word for this adverb in Mark and Matthew; Balanced and Readable use "ngay lúc đó", "ngay lập tức".
